text: Imagine that the electron in a hydrogen atom is replaced by a muon ($μ$). The mass of muon particle is 207 times that of an electron and charge is equal to the charge of an electron. The ionization potential of this hydrogen atom will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a hydrogen-like atom with a fixed nucleus, $E_{n}=-\dfrac{me^{4}}{8ε_{0}^{2}n^{2}h^{2}}$, so the ionization energy $|E_{1}|$ is proportional to the mass $m$ of the orbiting particle.

For the electron, $|E_{1}|=13.6\text{eV}$. With $m_{μ}=207m_{e}$:

$|E_{1}|_{μ}=207\times 13.6\text{eV}=2815.2\text{eV}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: In Young's double slit arrangement, slits are separated by a gap of 0.5 mm, and the screen is placed at a distance of 0.5 m from them. The distance between the first and the third bright fringe formed when the slits are illuminated by a monochromatic light of 5890 $A^{o}$ is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the double-slit experiment, the position of a bright fringe is given by the formula :

 $y=\frac{mλL}{d}$,

where :

m is the order of the fringe (1 for the first bright fringe, 2 for the second, etc.)
$λ$ is the wavelength of the light (in meters)
L is the distance from the slits to the screen (in meters)
d is the distance between the slits (in meters)

We need to find the difference in position between the first and third bright fringes. So, we find the position of both and subtract the position of the first from the position of the third :

$y_{3}=\frac{3λL}{d}$

$y_{1}=\frac{λL}{d}$

Then, the difference between the third and the first bright fringes is :

$y_{3}-y_{1}=2\frac{λL}{d}$

Now, let's plug the given values: $λ=5890\text{Å}=5890\times 10^{-10}m$ (since 1 Å = $10^{-10}$ meters), L = 0.5 m, and d = 0.5 mm = 0.5 $\times 10^{-3}$ m :

$y_{3}-y_{1}=2\times \frac{5890\times 10^{-10}\text{m}\times 0.5\text{m}}{0.5\times 10^{-3}\text{m}}=1178\times 10^{-6}\text{m}$

So, the correct answer is 1178 $\times 10^{-6}$ m, which corresponds to Option B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: In the experiment of Ohm's law, a potential difference of 5.0 V is applied across the end of a conductor of length 10.0 cm and diameter of 5.00 mm. The measured current in the conductor is 2.00 A. The maximum permissible percentage error in the resistivity of the conductor is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $V=IR=Iρ\dfrac{l}{A}$ with $A=\dfrac{πd^{2}}{4}$,

$ρ=\dfrac{πd^{2}V}{4Il}$

No uncertainties are stated, so each is taken as one unit in the last significant digit recorded: $\Delta V=0.1\text{V}$ (5.0 V), $\Delta l=0.1\text{cm}$ (10.0 cm), $\Delta d=0.01\text{mm}$ (5.00 mm) and $\Delta I=0.01\text{A}$ (2.00 A).

The maximum fractional error is the sum of the fractional errors, each multiplied by its power:

$\dfrac{\Delta ρ}{ρ}=2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d}+\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}+\dfrac{\Delta I}{I}+\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}=2\times \dfrac{0.01}{5.00}+\dfrac{0.1}{5.0}+\dfrac{0.01}{2.00}+\dfrac{0.1}{10.0}$

$\dfrac{\Delta ρ}{ρ}=0.004+0.020+0.005+0.010=0.039=3.9%$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

solution.body:

$\Rightarrow$ 2$π$f = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

text: The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius R is T. The period of another satellite in a circular orbit of radius 9R is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Kepler's Third Law states that the square of the period of a satellite's orbit is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit. This relationship can be written as:

$T^{2}\propto r^{3}$

where:

$T$ is the orbital period
$r$ is the radius of the circular orbit (which serves as the semi-major axis in this case)

Considering two satellites, one with period $T$ and radius $R$, and another with unknown period $T^{'}$ and radius $9R$, we can form an equation:

$\frac{T^{'}^{2}}{T^{2}}=\frac{(9R)^{3}}{R^{3}}$

This simplifies to:

$\frac{T^{'}^{2}}{T^{2}}=729$

Taking the square root of both sides, we get:

$T^{'}=T\times \sqrt{729}=T\times 27$

So, the period of another satellite in a circular orbit of radius $9R$ is $27T$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: Two separate wires A and B are stretched by 2 mm and 4 mm respectively, when they are subjected to a force of 2 N. Assume that both the wires are made up of same material and the radius of wire B is 4 times that of the radius of wire A. The length of the wires A and B are in the ratio of a : b. Then a/b can be expressed as 1/x where x is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ρ_{A}=ρ_{B}$

$r_{B}=4r_{A}$

$\Delta l_{a}=2$ mm

$\Delta l_{B}=4$ mm

$y=\frac{stress}{strain}=\frac{F/A}{\Delta l/l}$

$\Rightarrow$ y$\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{F}{A}$

$\Rightarrow$ $l=\frac{Ay\Delta l}{F}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{I_{a}}{I_{b}}=\frac{πr_{a}^{2}\times y\times \Delta I_{a}\times F}{πr_{b}^{2}\times y\times \Delta I_{b}\times F}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{I_{a}}{I_{b}}=\frac{r_{a}^{2}\times \Delta I_{a}}{r_{b}^{2}\times \Delta I_{b}}=\frac{r_{a}^{2}\times 2}{(4r_{a})^{2}\times 4}=\frac{r_{a}^{2}}{16r_{a}^{2}\times 2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{I_{a}}{I_{b}}=\frac{1}{32}$

$\therefore$ $x=32$

text:
A ball of mass 10 kg moving with a velocity 10$\sqrt{3}$ m/s along the x-axis, hits another ball of mass 20 kg which is at rest. After the collision, first ball comes to rest while the second ball disintegrates into two equal pieces. One piece starts moving along y-axis with a speed of 10 m/s. The second piece starts moving at an angle of 30${}^{\circ }$ with respect to the x-axis. The velocity of the ball moving at 30${}^{\circ }$ with x-axis is x m/s. The configuration of pieces after collision is shown in the figure below. The value of x to the nearest integer is $____________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Velocity of 10 kg ball = $v_{10}=10\sqrt{3}\hat{i}$

initial total momentum of system = $10\times 10\sqrt{3}\hat{i}$

Final total momentum of system

$=10\times 10\hat{j}+10\times x(\cos 30^{\circ }\hat{i}-\sin 30^{\circ }\hat{j})$

Now by conservation of momentum

$10\times 10\sqrt{3}\hat{i}=10\times 10\hat{j}+10\times x\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{i}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 20

text: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T=2π\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$. The measured value of the length of pendulum is 10 cm known to a 1mm accuracy. The time for 200 oscillations of the pendulum is found to be 100 second using a clock of 1s resolution. The percentage accuracy in the determination of 'g' using this pendulum is 'x'. The value of 'x' to be nearest integer is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$T=2π\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$

$T^{2}=4π^{2}\left (\frac{l}{g}\right )$

$g=4π^{2}\frac{l}{T^{2}}$

$\frac{\Delta g}{g}=\frac{\Delta l}{l}+\frac{2\Delta T}{T}$

$\frac{\Delta g}{g}=\frac{1\times 10^{-3}}{1\times 10^{-1}}+\frac{2\times 1}{100}$

$\frac{\Delta g}{g}=0.02+0.01=0.03$

$100\times \frac{\Delta g}{g}=0.03\times 100=3%$

$\frac{\Delta g}{g}\times 100=3%$
